2. seated exactly as the first figure, every line the same, the eyes closed in a blink: each eye a short downward-curved ink line.
3. seated on the stool exactly as in the first figure, the head a quarter turned toward the viewer's right, talking to a neighbour at the picture's right, the mouth open in a glad smile.
The person, as described: The people are the base filler cast dressed in the story crowd kit: the four plain, never-named grown people of the Bible's own time kept in the library as base sizes and genders (`filler-bases`, kept poses), drawn once more in their kept stance, place and size, each wearing the kit's house parts over an unchanged body (in-its-order item 3), so a film's crowd takes its headcloths, veils, mantles and beards from this sheet and dyes them to any story cloth.
